newsitem.title: COMOROS: Twenty on trial in Comoros for football murders.
newsitem.headline: Twenty on trial in Comoros for football murders.

text.p: Twenty villagers accused of murdering four rival supporters after a football match turned violent went on trial on Saturday in the Comoro Islands.
Said Ali Mohamed, leader of the 20 accused from the village of Chezami, was the first to appear in court in Moroni and pleaded not guilty to involvement in killing the villagers from Hamtsimdzi.
Reading the charges, the court clerk said one of the dead was 18-year-old student Charif Said Cheikh who had his right leg, tongue and genitals hacked off in the attack on July 21.

Prosecutors say the 20 Chezami villagers savagely attacked Hamtsimdzi residents with knives and machetes after a football match between the villages was stopped because a fight broke out among rival supporters while Hamtsimdzi was leading.
Following the killings, President Mohamed Taki cut off all government services to Chezami, barred its residents from voting in elections and vowed those who had killed would be killed.
The 20 face the death penalty if they are convicted of murder by the court in the capital Moroni. There is no appeal.
Only Taki as president can pardon those sentenced to death. He refused in September to pardon a 25-year-old man who murdered a pregnant woman. Ali Youssouf was publicly executed by firing squad.

The previous public execution in Comoros was in 1978. The Hamtsimdzi killings shocked the Indian Ocean island archipelago which has had up to 17 attempted coups since independence from France in 1975.
